items.title: Finite unrolled domains and outputs are Borel

references.title: Terence Tao, An Introduction to Measure Theory, preliminary full-text book
references.locator: Chapter 1, §1.4, Remark 1.4.33, printed p. 96 / PDF p. 111: composition of measurable morphisms is measurable.

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the proof is finite induction over explicitly supplied layers.
items.statement:
Let $n,m\ge1$, $X=\mathbb R^n$, and let $\Omega$ be a Borel subset of $\mathbb R^{m\times n}\times\mathbb R^m$ with its relative Borel sigma-algebra. Equip $\Omega\times X$ with the finite product sigma-algebra $\mathcal B(\Omega)\otimes\mathcal B(X)$. Fix an integer $N\ge0$, real parameters $\tau_0,\ldots,\tau_{N-1}$, a Borel initialization $I:\Omega\to X$, Borel sets $D_k\subseteq\Omega\times X$, and Borel maps $B_k:D_k\to X$ for $0\le k<N$, where each $D_k$ carries its relative product sigma-algebra. For $p=(A,y)\in\Omega$ and $x\in X$, define $c(p,x)=A^{\mathsf T}(y-Ax)$. Set $E_0=\Omega$ and $x_0=I$; recursively, for $0\le k<N$, set

$$E_{k+1}:=\{p\in E_k:(p,x_k(p)+\tau_k c(p,x_k(p)))\in D_k\},\qquad x_{k+1}(p):=B_k(p,x_k(p)+\tau_k c(p,x_k(p)))\quad(p\in E_{k+1}).$$

Then every $E_k$ is a Borel subset of $\Omega$ and every $x_k:E_k\to X$ is Borel. In particular, $E_N$ is exactly the set of inputs where all $N$ updates are defined, and the finite output map $x_N:E_N\to X$ is Borel.

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; all recurrences, finite laws, and scalar witnesses are explicit.
items.statement:
Let $N\ge1$ and let $\Phi_{\theta,N}$ be the point-valued map obtained by an initialization followed by $N$ defined, fixed-parameter update maps on an admissible input $(A,y)$. This finite definition does not imply that the iterates of an underlying infinite recurrence converge: even the repeated scalar update $T(x)=2x$ is defined at every finite depth from $x_0=1$, while $T^k(x_0)=2^k$ diverges.

For squared reconstruction loss $\ell(t,a)=\|a-t\|_2^2$ on the signal space, let $\mathcal S=\{(A_i,y_i,x_i^\dagger)\}_{i=1}^s$ be a nonempty finite training set, $s\ge1$, and let $P_{\mathcal S}=s^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^s\delta_{((A_i,y_i),x_i^\dagger)}$ be its empirical joint law. The training-law risk is $L_{\mathcal S}(\theta)=R_{P_{\mathcal S}}(\Phi_{\theta,N})$, where $R_P(g)$ is the expected loss of the Borel point rule $g$ under the joint input-target law $P$. Under an operator and data shift, the forward residual is $\|A\Phi_{\theta,N}(A,y)-y\|_2$, and for a test probability law $Q$ on the same input-target space the test risk is $R_Q(\theta)=R_Q(\Phi_{\theta,N})$ when this expectation is defined. No bound on either quantity follows from a bound on $L_{\mathcal S}$ alone: for every $M>0$ there is a one-sample scalar training law with zero training-law risk and a shifted scalar operator with forward residual and squared test risk both greater than $M$.

For a recurrence $z_{k+1}=G(z_k,\theta)$, a fixed point at parameter $\theta$ is a state $z_*(\theta)$ satisfying $G(z_*(\theta),\theta)=z_*(\theta)$. If the initialization and update maps are continuously differentiable in their state and trainable-parameter variables on open neighborhoods of their visited inputs, automatic differentiation through the deployed graph computes the derivative of that finite map. It does not replace that derivative by the derivative of a limiting fixed point. In particular, for $G(z,\theta)=qz+(1-q)\theta$ with $0<q<1$, $z_0(\theta)=0$, and $\theta_0=0$, each finite iterate has zero fixed-point residual while its parameter derivative differs from the exact fixed-point derivative.

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is assumed only because the cited Landweber interface states it; the scalar calculations use no choice and do not assume the full Axiom of Choice.
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $X=Y=\mathbb R$, let $A x=ax$ for a fixed $a>0$, and let the exact datum be $y=ax^\dagger$ with $x^\dagger\ne0$ and noise bound $\delta=0$. Choose $N\ge1$ and $0<\omega a^2<1$. The exact Landweber prefix starts at $x_0=0$ and uses $x_{k+1}=x_k+\omega a(y-ax_k)$ through its finite budget $N$. For a learned finite-depth architecture with zero initialization, identity update blocks, and layer parameters $\widetilde\omega_0,\ldots,\widetilde\omega_{N-1}$, the updates are $\widetilde x_{k+1}=\widetilde x_k+\widetilde\omega_k a(y-a\widetilde x_k)$. If every $\widetilde\omega_k=\omega$, the two depth-$N$ outputs coincide; otherwise the learned output is the finite composition determined by its own layer parameters.

items.axiom_use: No choice axiom is used; the training and test laws are explicit finite probability measures.
items.statement: Let $X=Y=\mathbb R$ and consider the one-step learned update $F_\theta(a,y)=\theta ay$ on the declared domain of all scalar operator/data pairs. For a Borel point rule $g$ and a joint input-target probability law $P$, define squared risk by $R_P(g)=\int |g(a,y)-x^\dagger|^2\,P(d((a,y),x^\dagger))$. Let $P_\mathcal S$ be the probability law assigning mass one to $((a,y),x^\dagger)=((1,1),1)$, and let $Q_t$ assign mass one to $((a,y),x^\dagger)=((t,t),1)$ for each shift $t>1$. Define the training risk $L_\mathcal S(\theta)=R_{P_\mathcal S}(F_\theta)$ and the test risk $R_{Q_t}(\theta)=R_{Q_t}(F_\theta)$. The forward residual is $r_t=|tF_\theta(t,t)-t|$. The assertion refuted is that some finite constant $C$ bounds both $r_t$ and $R_{Q_t}(\theta)$ for every $t>1$ whenever $L_\mathcal S(\theta)=0$.
